In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the e-cloud and the beam instability, with the development of the diagnostics tools and with the evaluation of the effectiveness of the different devices used to control the e-cloud and beam instabilities.
the development of a set of diagnostics tools, both hardware and software, to monitor in real time and to evaluate the beam instabilities and their control in the DAFNA positron ring.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the e-cloud instabilities are now under control in the DAFNA positron ring, with the bunch-by-buch feedback system playing a fundamental role.
all these tools have been very useful and necessary to achieve the best beam conditions and the highest luminosity in DAFNE.

the clearing electrodes have been the best and most powerful solution, but they need to be properly set in order to avoid the beam blow-up in collision, which is a delicate task that needs to be done in a short time window.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the e-cloud clearing electrodes have been very effective in controlling the instabilities and the solenoids have been very useful to keep the e-cloud level low, but the feedback systems have been essential for the beam operation.

, thanks to the adopted measures, we have been able to run with the positron beam in DAFNE with an average beam lifetime of about 2 hours, with a maximum beam current of about 2.5 mA and with a bunch-by-bunch current spread lower than 1% (rms).

the bunch-by-b bunch feedback systems have proved to be the most effective tool in the control of e-cloud instabilities, but that the solenoids around straights have been the most powerful tool in the mitigation of the instabilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bunch-by-buchn diagnostics is a very powerful tool to understand the e-cloud instabilities and to optimize the clearing electrode configuration.

the clearing electrode system is a powerful tool to mitigate e-cloud instabilities and that the best way to set up the system is to make a dedicated tuning procedure, using bunch-by-bunch data, before starting to collide.
the bunch-by-b bunch feedback system is an extremely powerful and flexible tool for beam instabilities studies and diagnostics.
